idea: Add the shrinking variant to the same search: replace an (m+1)×(m+1) block of cells by an m×m grid of squares of side (m+1)/(mk). This removes 2m+1 squares at a cost of (m+1)/k, so a larger k can be used when n sits just below a perfect square (e.g. n=6, 8, 11, 13, 15). Take the maximum over both variants and all k.
